sections.what: The Rose provides breast screening and diagnostic care through Houston-area centers and mobile units. Its patient navigators help uninsured patients arrange cancer treatment and practical support. Sponsored care, translation, transport and childcare assistance seek to reduce barriers from diagnosis through recovery.
sections.monitoring: FY2025 annual report page 22 reports 8,571 uninsured patients, 400 patients diagnosed with cancer, 415 cancers and 187 patients navigated into treatment. The 3,476 navigation interactions are not unique additional patients. Request distinct local households, time to treatment, alternative-provider uptake, stage, false-positive workups, overdiagnosis and patient cost incidence. Screening services and treatment navigation may overlap; no added grand-total cohort is used.
sections.qualitative: The current annual report distinguishes diagnosed patients, treatment navigation and repeated interactions. Original current returns establish a full annual recognized recipient cost. BCCS navigation and practical assistance provide concrete care-access and household-resource mechanisms. Treatment navigation is not a measured additional cancer-stage or survival improvement. Local utility, household resources and screening harms remain unsupported numerical priors. Geography, outside treatment costs and marginal capacity are not fully established. Original FY2025 Form 990 verifies EIN 76-0193812. Recipient-owned giving route was checked without a transaction. The July matching appeal is stale and receives no numerical credit.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $42.02 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 4.008925 clinical QALYs and -0.204127 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.002380 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $15,986,247. The 8,571 uninsured patients form a wider exposure reference with judged .95 household mapping and .25 annual additional response. The 187 treatment navigations are hypothesized within that group, not confirmed uninsured household deduplication: .95 mapping times .25 response times .3 clinically beneficial treatment change gives 13.32375 trajectories. A weak .2 utility change lasts two finite discounted years, not lifetime survival. All 2,035.6125 exposed households incur a judged full $20 incremental process/travel/foregone-pay burden, plus .0001 one-off clinical harm each for possible false-positive/overdiagnosis effects. Independent .1 resource success receives $300 net aid/transport/childcare resources after taxes, benefit offsets and alternative support; positive overlap .5 yields $130 net, while others lose $20. Union 2035.6125 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 13.32375; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $20,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. Externally funded BCCS/hospital treatment costs are not captured by the recipient budget and are unknown, not zero. Provider and displaced-payer stresses are separate additional opportunity costs, not another identical charge for donations already in cost. Household aid is a transfer rather than new social production. No ordinary survivor earnings or retail treatment price is counted. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: FY2025 original expense $15,866,042 plus $120,205 netted event cost gives $15,986,247. FY2024 $16,471,873 plus $96,459 gives $16,568,332. FY2023 $15,265,960 plus $81,601 gives $15,347,561. Expense-side Schedule D removed expenses are zero in these returns; no populated rental-expense addback recovered. Partner treatment and unrecognized volunteers remain unknown. Paid clinical revenue, BCCS and CPRIT grants are baseline funding, not proof of gift-driven expansion.

model.costScope: Full annual recognized recipient cost against limited uninsured screening/navigation hypothesis, not whole portfolio EV or marginal offer
model.geographicAttribution: Houston centers plus extensive Southeast Texas mobile delivery; .8 local share judged, not observed MSA residence
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Existing insurance, BCCS, Harris Health, other screening/navigation providers and family support retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Additional timely appropriate breast treatment with screening harms; screening counts and diagnoses are not causal QALYs
